reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
There are several ways of arranging the tiles so that they form patterns. The grid below has been shaded to show how tiles can be placed on some of the squares. The pattern can be continued so that AB and CD are lines of symmetry.

[Image: A 4 by 4 grid with symmetry axes AB and CD]

Shade in all the remaining squares on the grid so that the resulting pattern is symmetrical about line AB, and also is symmetrical about line CD.

descriptors: Both quadrants correctly shaded (pattern shaded or demarcated in some way making symmetrical pattern about both axes, AB and CD).
One of the two quadrants correctly shaded.
Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task).

reference_items.figure_description:
A 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line AB (with A at the top, B at the bottom) and a horizontal line CD (with C at the left, D at the right).
Two quadrants are shaded with tile patterns:
- Top-right 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 1-2, columns 3-4):
  - Row 1, column 3: small black square in the top-left corner.
  - Row 1, column 4: small black square in the top-right corner.
  - Row 2, column 3: small black square in the bottom-left corner.
  - Row 2, column 4: small black square in the bottom-right corner.
  - In the center of this 2-by-2 quadrant (where the four squares meet), a large black diamond (rotated square) is formed across the inner corners of all four squares.
- Bottom-left 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 3-4, columns 1-2):
  - Shaded with the exact same pattern: four small black corner squares at the outer corners of the 2-by-2 quadrant, and a large black diamond centered where the four squares meet.
The top-left 2-by-2 quadrant and bottom-right 2-by-2 quadrant are entirely blank (unshaded).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.

reference_items.figure_description:
Four labeled options (A, B, C, D):
- Option A shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The two squares in the first column and the two squares in the fifth column are completely shaded black (4 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option B shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. The top-left square (row 1, column 1) and bottom-right square (row 2, column 5) are shaded black (2 of 10 squares shaded).
- Option C shows a rectangle divided into a 2-by-5 grid of 10 equal squares. In the top row, the 1st, 3rd, and 5th squares are shaded black; in the bottom row, the 2nd and 4th squares are shaded black (5 of 10 squares shaded in a checkerboard pattern).
- Option D shows a rectangular box containing five small circles scattered inside: two circles are solid black and three circles are open white circles with a black outline.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D are shown in a row. Each tile is divided conceptually into four smaller quadrants:
- Tile A: A shaded black triangle in the upper-left corner (formed by the diagonal connecting the midpoint of the top edge and the midpoint of the left edge) and a solid black square in the lower-right quadrant.
- Tile B: A shaded black triangle in the upper-right corner and a solid black square in the lower-left quadrant.
- Tile C: A solid black square in the upper-left quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-right corner.
- Tile D: A solid black square in the upper-right quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-left corner.

Below is a 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line PQ and a horizontal line RS. P is at the top of the vertical line, Q is at the bottom; R is at the left of the horizontal line, S is at the right. Four squares are already labeled:
- Row 1 (top), column 1 (left): 'D'
- Row 2, column 4 (right): 'C'
- Row 3, column 2: 'B'
- Row 4 (bottom), column 3: 'A'
The remaining 12 squares are blank.

reference_items.stem:
Pat has red tiles and black tiles. Pat uses the tiles to make square shapes.

The 3 × 3 shape has 1 black tile and 8 red tiles.
[Image: A black tile in the middle, surrounded by the 8 red tiles, to make a square shape.]

The 4 × 4 shape has 4 black tiles and 12 red tiles.
[Image: Four black tiles forming a square in the center, with 12 red tiles lining the sides, to create a larger square shape.]

The table below shows the number of tiles for the first three shapes Pat made. Pat continued making shapes using this pattern. Complete the table for the 6 × 6 and 7 × 7 shapes.

| Shape | Number of Black Tiles | Number of Red Tiles | Total Number of Tiles |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 3 × 3 | 1 | 8 | 9 |
| 4 × 4 | 4 | 12 | 16 |
| 5 × 5 | 9 | 16 | 25 |
| 6 × 6 | 16 | | |
| 7 × 7 | 25 | | |

descriptors:
Both rows completely correct
Shape 6 x 6: 20, 36
Shape 7 x 7: 24, 49
Entries for one row correct but not both

Entries for one column correct but not both
Red Tiles: 20, 24   OR   Total Tiles: 36, 49
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
